q: Even when you have the right-of-way, what are you still responsible for?
choices: Proceeding first so other drivers know what to expect
Doing everything you can to prevent a collision
Sounding your horn before entering the intersection
Nothing more, since the other driver must yield
hint: Having the right-of-way does not end your duty to drive safely.
explain: Right-of-way rules tell you who should yield, but you must still do everything you can to avoid a collision.
quote: However, even if you have the right-of-way, you are still responsible to do everything you can to prevent a collision.

q: Your traffic light is green, but a police officer directing traffic signals you to stop. What must you do?
choices: Proceed, because the green light comes first
Proceed slowly and sound your horn
Stop, because the officer's direction comes before the signal
Stop only if other vehicles are in the intersection
hint: Think about who outranks a sign or a light.
explain: Directions given by a peace officer or police officer must be followed over traffic signs or signals.
quote: Directions given by a peace officer or police officer must be followed over traffic signs or signals.

q: What does a stop sign require you to do?
choices: Come to a complete stop, check for pedestrians and traffic, then go when safe
Slow down, and continue without stopping if no one is coming
Stop only if there are vehicles on the cross street
Stop only if a pedestrian is waiting to cross the street
hint: A rolling stop is not a stop.
explain: At a stop sign you must come to a complete stop, check the intersection carefully, and go only when it is safe.
quote: A stop sign indicates that your vehicle must come to a complete stop. After stopping, check the intersection carefully for pedestrians and other traffic. When safe, you may proceed.

q: You come to a stop sign where a stop line is painted on the road. Where must your vehicle stop?
choices: With the front wheels on the stop line
Past the stop line, at the edge of the cross street
Before the stop line
Anywhere within 15 metres of the stop line
hint: The painted line marks a limit you should not cross.
explain: Where a stop line is marked, you must come to a complete stop before it.
quote: Where a stop line has been marked, bring your vehicle to a complete stop before the stop line.

q: At a stop sign there is no stop line, but there is a marked crosswalk. Where do you stop?
choices: In the marked crosswalk, so you can see better
Past the crosswalk, at the edge of the cross street
Within 30 metres of the crosswalk
Before the marked crosswalk
hint: Pedestrians need that painted area kept clear.
explain: When there is no stop line, you must stop before the marked crosswalk.
quote: Where there is no stop line, stop before the marked crosswalk.

q: At a stop sign with no stop line and no marked crosswalk, the rule says you must stop within what distance of the intersecting road?
choices: Within 3 metres
Within 10 metres
Within 15 metres
Within 30 metres
hint: Close enough to see cross traffic, but not blocking people who are crossing.
explain: With no stop line or marked crosswalk, you must stop within three metres (10 feet) of the intersecting roadway, where you will not block pedestrians.
quote: If there is no stop line or marked crosswalk at the intersection, you must stop within three metres (10 feet) of the intersecting roadway.

q: At a four-way stop, several vehicles arrive at different times. Which vehicle should go first?
choices: The vehicle on the far left
The vehicle going straight through
The largest vehicle
The vehicle that arrived first
hint: Think first come, first served.
explain: At three- and four-way stops, courtesy is to let the vehicle that arrived first go first.
quote: Courtesy is to allow the vehicle that arrived first to proceed first.

q: You and another driver arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. The other vehicle is on your right. Who should go first?
choices: You, because you are on the left
The vehicle on your right
Whichever driver signals first
Whichever driver is going straight
hint: The same side gets priority at intersections that have no signs at all.
explain: If two vehicles arrive at the same time, courtesy allows the vehicle on the right to go first.
quote: If two vehicles arrive at the same time, courtesy allows the vehicle on the right to proceed first.

q: What does a yield sign mean?
choices: You must let vehicles that do not face a yield sign go first
You must always come to a complete stop
You have the right-of-way over cross traffic
You must speed up to merge ahead of traffic
hint: The sign is about giving way, not about being in charge.
explain: A yield sign means you must let vehicles that do not face a yield sign proceed first. Slow down and be ready to stop.
quote: A yield sign means that you must allow other vehicles that do not face a yield sign the right-of-way to proceed.

q: You reach a yield sign and there is no traffic and no pedestrians you need to yield to. What may you do?
choices: You must still come to a complete stop
Stop and count to three before going
Go through without coming to a complete stop
Sound your horn, then go
hint: A yield sign is not the same as a stop sign.
explain: If there is no one you must yield to, you may go through without a complete stop, at a speed that still lets you stop easily.
quote: If there are no pedestrians or traffic that you are required to yield to, you may proceed through the intersection without coming to a complete stop.

q: At an intersection with no signs and no traffic lights, which vehicle must you yield to?
choices: A vehicle on your left
The vehicle travelling faster
The vehicle on the wider road
A vehicle on your right
hint: It is the same side that gets courtesy when two vehicles reach a four-way stop together.
explain: At uncontrolled intersections, you must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle on your right.
quote: Some intersections have no traffic signs and no traffic signal lights. At these intersections, you must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle on your right.
topic: Uncontrolled intersection: yield to vehicle on the right

q: You are approaching an intersection with no signs or signals, and parked cars block your view of the cross street. What should you do?
choices: Keep your speed so you clear the intersection quickly
Speed up to get through before anyone arrives
Sound your horn and keep going at the same speed
Reduce your speed enough to be able to stop easily
hint: If you cannot see what is coming, you need room to react.
explain: When your view is blocked, you must slow down enough to stop your vehicle easily. Slow down even more on slippery roads.
quote: Your view may be obstructed by fences, trees, or parked cars. You must reduce your speed enough to be able to stop your vehicle easily.

q: At a T intersection with no signs or signals, you are driving straight through along the top of the T. A vehicle is approaching on the side road to your right. Who has the right-of-way?
choices: You do, because you are going straight through
The driver on the side road, who is on your right
You do, because you are on the through road
Whichever driver is moving faster
hint: There are no signs here, so the usual rule for uncontrolled intersections applies.
explain: With no signs or signals, the driver on the right has the right-of-way, even at a T intersection. The driver going straight must not assume they have it.
quote: There are no traffic control signs or signals, therefore the driver on the right (vehicle B) has the right-of-way. Be careful in this situation in case the driver going straight through (vehicle A) incorrectly assumes the right-of-way.

q: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you want to turn left. A car is coming straight toward you from the opposite direction. Who must yield?
choices: The oncoming car, because you signalled first
The oncoming car, because you arrived first
You, because you would be crossing its path
Neither, since you are not on each other's right
hint: The driver whose turn cuts across the other's lane has to wait.
explain: A driver turning left across the path of an approaching vehicle must wait until it is safe. Neither vehicle is to the right of the other, so the turning driver yields.
quote: A yields to B: A would be crossing B's path and neither is to the right of the other. ... A driver turning left across the path of an approaching vehicle cannot turn left until it is safe.
topic: Left turns: yield to oncoming traffic

q: You are driving out of an alley onto a main street, and a sidewalk crosses the alley exit. What must you do?
choices: Stop before the sidewalk, stop again before the street, and yield to pedestrians
Slow down at the sidewalk, and come to a full stop only at the street
Stop at the sidewalk only if a pedestrian is walking on it
Sound your horn and enter the street slowly without stopping
hint: Think about both the people walking and the traffic on the street.
explain: When leaving an alley, driveway, parking lot or service road, you must stop before any sidewalk crossing, stop before entering the main street, and yield to pedestrians.
quote: When exiting from service roads, alleys, parking lots, and driveways, you must: stop before any sidewalk crossing stop before entering a main street yield to pedestrians.

q: Do right-of-way rules apply in a parking lot?
choices: No, parking lots are private property
Only where a stop sign is posted
Yes, parking lot intersections without signs follow the right-of-way rules
Only when a parking attendant is present
hint: Where two parking lot lanes cross, that is still an intersection.
explain: Parking lots have intersections without signs or signals, and the normal right-of-way rules apply.
quote: Parking lots have intersections without signs or signals, and the right-of-way rules apply.

q: The car in the lane beside you stops at an intersection to let a pedestrian cross. There is no painted crosswalk. What must you do?
choices: Pass it carefully, since the crosswalk is not marked
Stay behind it and do not pass it
Pass it if the pedestrian is not yet in your lane
Sound your horn and pass slowly
hint: Every intersection has crosswalks, even ones without paint.
explain: All intersections have crosswalks, marked or unmarked, and you must not pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian.
quote: All intersections have crosswalks that may be marked or unmarked and you must not pass another vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian.
topic: Do not pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian

q: Your light is green, but traffic on the far side of the intersection is backed up. When should you enter the intersection?
choices: Right away, because your light is green
When you can get at least halfway across
As soon as the car ahead of you starts moving
Only when you can completely clear the intersection and the far crosswalk
hint: Think about the cross traffic when your light turns red.
explain: Do not enter an intersection until you can completely clear it and the crosswalk on the other side. Stopping inside blocks cross traffic and pedestrians.
quote: If traffic is delayed at an intersection, do not enter the intersection until you can completely clear the intersection and crosswalk on the other side.
topic: Do not enter intersection unless you can clear it

q: In which direction does traffic travel around a roundabout or traffic circle?
choices: Clockwise
Counterclockwise
Either direction, whichever is shorter
Clockwise for cars and counterclockwise for trucks
hint: Picture the hands of a clock, then think about which way you circle the island.
explain: Traffic always circulates counterclockwise around the centre island.
quote: Traffic always circulates in a counterclockwise direction around a centre island.

q: You are entering a roundabout. Who must you yield to?
choices: Traffic waiting to enter on your right
No one, because traffic in the circle must yield to you
Traffic already in the circle
Only large trucks in the circle
hint: Think about who is already moving around the island.
explain: Vehicles entering a roundabout or traffic circle must yield to traffic already in the circle.
quote: Vehicles entering the intersection must yield to traffic already in the circle.
topic: Roundabouts: yield to traffic in circle

q: How is a roundabout different from a traffic circle?
choices: It has a larger centre island so traffic can go faster
It has a smaller centre island and a tighter curve to keep speeds lower
Traffic in it travels clockwise instead of counterclockwise
Drivers entering it have the right-of-way over drivers in it
hint: The design is meant to slow you down.
explain: A roundabout has a smaller centre island than a traffic circle and a tighter curve that encourages lower speeds.
quote: The centre island of a roundabout is smaller than the centre island of a traffic circle. The roundabout has been designed with a tighter curve around the island to encourage lower speeds

q: You are in a roundabout and plan to leave at the third exit. When should you turn on your right signal?
choices: Before you enter the circle
As soon as you are in the circle
After you pass the exit just before the one you want
After you have left the circle
hint: The signal should tell others you are leaving at the very next exit.
explain: Wait until you have passed the exit before your intended exit, then signal right. This tells others you will leave at the next exit.
quote: Always wait to activate your right turn signal after passing the exit that is before your intended exit. This tells other drivers that you intend to leave the circle at the next exit.

q: You will take the first exit from a one-lane roundabout. How should you signal?
choices: Signal right as you approach and leave it on until you have exited
Signal left as you approach, then right once inside
Do not signal at all, since it is the first exit
Signal right only after you pass the first exit
hint: You are leaving almost as soon as you enter.
explain: For the first exit, use your right signal as you approach and keep it on until you have left the circle.
quote: When you intend to exit at the first available exit: Use your right signal as you approach. Leave it on until you have exited the circle.

q: In a two-lane roundabout, which lane should you use to enter if you plan to go past the first exit?
choices: The right lane
The left lane
Either lane, then switch lanes inside the circle
The right lane, then move left once inside
hint: Your lane choice depends on how far around the circle you are going.
explain: Drivers planning to travel past the first exit should use the left lane to enter and exit.
quote: Drivers planning to travel past the first exit should use the left lane to enter and exit.

q: In a two-lane roundabout, you want to take the first exit. Which lane should you approach and exit in?
choices: The left lane
Either lane
Enter in the left lane and exit in the right lane
The right lane
hint: The first exit is the closest one.
explain: For the first exit, approach the circle using the right lane, yield to traffic in the circle, and exit using the right lane.
quote: Approach the circle using the right lane. ... Exit the circle using the right lane.

q: You are driving in the right lane of a two-lane roundabout and want to move into the left lane. What should you do?
choices: Signal and change to the left lane when there is a gap
Stay in your lane, because you must not change lanes in the circle
Stop in the circle, then move over when the left lane is clear
Speed up and cut into the left lane
hint: Lane choice in a roundabout is made before you enter.
explain: Do not change lanes in the circle. Pick your lane before you enter, and stay in it until you exit.
quote: Do not change lanes in the circle.

q: Inside a two-lane roundabout, which drivers must yield?
choices: Drivers in the right lane yield to drivers in the left lane
Drivers in the left lane yield to drivers in the right lane
Drivers in the circle yield to drivers entering it
No one yields once inside the circle
hint: Inside-lane drivers must cross the outside lane to leave.
explain: While in the circle, drivers on the right must yield to drivers on the left. Left-lane drivers exit across the right lane, so use caution.
quote: While in the circle, the drivers on the right must yield to the drivers on the left.

q: You are in a roundabout and cannot exit safely at your planned exit. What should you do?
choices: Turn around and drive clockwise back to it
Change lanes quickly and exit anyway
Back up to the exit you missed
Stay in your lane and go around the circle again
hint: A circle has no end, so there is always another chance.
explain: If you cannot stop or exit safely, stay in your lane and travel around the circle again.
quote: If you cannot stop or exit safely, stay in your lane and travel around the circle/ roundabout again.

q: How far before an intersection should you be in the proper lane for your turn?
choices: At least 3 metres
At least 150 metres
At least 300 metres
At least 15 metres
hint: It is the same distance for both left and right turns.
explain: Prepare for a turn well in advance. You should be in your proper turning lane at least 15 metres (50 feet) before the intersection.
quote: You should be in your proper turning lane at least 15 metres (50 feet) before the intersection.

q: When turning right from a two-way road onto another two-way road, where should your vehicle be?
choices: Centred in the lane, not more than 1 metre from the curb or road's edge
Straddling the curb lane and the lane beside it
In the left part of the lane, about 3 metres from the curb
Near the centre of the road, close to the yellow line
hint: Stay close to the right side of the road through the whole turn.
explain: Stay centred in the turning lane, not more than one metre (three feet) from the curb or road's edge, before, during, and after the turn.
quote: When making a right turn from a two-way road onto another two-way road, stay centred in the turning lane, not more than one metre (three feet) away from the curb or road's edge.

q: You are turning right and pedestrians are crossing the street you are turning onto. When may you enter that crosswalk?
choices: When the pedestrians reach the middle of the road
As soon as your light turns green
When the pedestrians are safely out of the intersection
After you sound your horn and they stop
hint: Pedestrians in the crosswalk come first.
explain: Yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk, and do not enter the crosswalk to turn until they are safely out of the intersection.
quote: Yield to pedestrians crossing in the crosswalk. Do not enter the crosswalk to turn until pedestrians are safely out of the intersection.

q: You are turning right, and a car is parked in the curb lane close to the corner of the street you are turning onto. Where should you turn?
choices: Into the curb lane, then stop behind the parked car
Into the first available lane to the left of the parked car
Into the far left lane of the new street
Into the curb lane, then swerve around the parked car
hint: There is no room to finish the turn in the first lane.
explain: If the first lane has a parked car or obstruction close to the corner, turn into the first available lane to the left of it. Yield to traffic coming from your left in that lane.
quote: If the first lane on the street you are turning onto has a parked car or obstruction close to the corner, turn into the first available lane to the left of the parked vehicle.

q: Unless a sign prohibits it, when may you turn right on a red light?
choices: After coming to a complete stop at the stop line or crosswalk
After slowing down and checking for traffic
Only when a green arrow is showing
Never, you must wait for a green light
hint: A red light still means stop first.
explain: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn right on a red light after a complete stop at the proper stopping point, when it is safe.
quote: Unless prohibited by a sign, you may turn right on a red light after you come to a complete stop at the proper stopping point (stop line or crosswalk).

q: You have moved into the intersection and are waiting for a chance to turn left. How should your front wheels be pointed?
choices: Turned to the left, ready to go
Turned to the right, toward the curb
Straight ahead
Turned slightly left so others know you are turning
hint: Think about what would happen if someone hit you from behind.
explain: Stay to the right of the yellow line with your front wheels straight. If you are hit from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.
quote: If you must stop in the intersection prior to completing a left turn, stay to the right of the yellow line and keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead. Doing so prevents the vehicle from being pushed into oncoming traffic if you are hit from behind.
topic: Left turns: wheels straight while waiting

q: Before you turn left off a two-lane highway, what check should you make?
choices: A right shoulder check for cyclists
A look at the oncoming lane only, with no shoulder check
A shoulder check to the left, to be sure no one is passing you
A glance at the rear-view mirror only
hint: On a highway, someone may be overtaking you on the side you are turning toward.
explain: Before turning left off a two-lane highway, do a left shoulder check to be sure another vehicle is not passing you on your left.
quote: Before turning left off a two-lane highway, do a shoulder check to the left to be sure you are not being passed by another vehicle on your left.

q: You are turning left from a two-way road onto another two-way road. Which lane should you turn into?
choices: The lane nearest the right curb
The lane nearest and to the right of the yellow line
The first lane on the left side of the road
Any lane that happens to be clear
hint: Finish on the correct side of the centre line, in the closest lane.
explain: Turn from the lane nearest and to the right of the yellow line, into the lane nearest and to the right of the yellow line.
quote: When it is safe and legal, turn from the lane nearest and to the right of the yellow line. Turn into the lane nearest and to the right of the yellow line.

q: You are turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road. Which lane should you turn into?
choices: The lane nearest the right side of the road
The middle lane
The first available lane on the left side of the road
Any lane, as long as you signal
hint: Pick the lane closest to where your turn begins.
explain: Turn from the lane nearest the yellow line into the first available lane on the left side of the one-way road.
quote: When it is safe and legal, turn from the lane nearest the yellow line. Turn into the first available lane on the left side of the road.

q: You are on a one-way street and want to turn left onto a two-way street. Which lane should you turn from?
choices: The lane nearest the left side of the road
The lane nearest the right side of the road
The middle lane
Any lane, as long as you signal
hint: Start the turn as close as you can to the side you are turning toward.
explain: Turn from the lane nearest the left side of the one-way road, into the nearest lane to the right of the yellow line.
quote: When it is safe and legal, turn from the lane nearest the left side of the road. Turn into the nearest lane to the right of the yellow line.

q: You are turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street. Which lane should you turn into?
choices: The lane nearest the right side of the road
The lane nearest the left side of the road
The middle lane
Whichever lane has the least traffic
hint: Both the start and the end of this turn hug the same side.
explain: Turn from the lane nearest the left side of the road into the lane nearest the left side of the new road.
quote: When it is safe and legal, turn from the lane nearest the left side of the road. Turn into the lane nearest to the left side of the road.

q: If no sign prohibits it, when may you turn left on a red light?
choices: From a two-way street onto a one-way street, after a complete stop
From a one-way street onto another one-way street, after a complete stop
From a two-way street onto a two-way street, after a complete stop
From any street, if you slow down and no traffic is coming
hint: Both the street you leave and the street you enter matter.
explain: If no sign prohibits it, you may turn left on red from a one-way onto another one-way after a complete stop at the proper stopping point, when it is safe. Yield to pedestrians crossing to your left.
quote: When the light is red, if there are no signs prohibiting turning, you may turn left from a one-way onto another one-way after coming to a complete stop at the proper stopping location (stop line or crosswalk) and the turn can be completed safely.

q: You are making a left turn at an intersection with dual left turn lanes. What should you do?
choices: Swing wide to give the vehicle beside you more room
Change to the other lane during the turn if it looks clearer
Turn into whichever lane on the new street is emptiest
Turn into the lane that corresponds to the lane you turned from
hint: Another vehicle may be turning alongside you.
explain: At dual lane turns, approach in one of the marked lanes and turn into the corresponding lane. Never swing wide or change lanes, as another vehicle could be turning beside you.
quote: approach the intersection in one of the marked lanes and turn into the corresponding lane. ... Never swing wide or change lanes in dual lane turn intersections as another vehicle could be turning beside you.

q: After a dual lane turn, the two turning lanes merge into one. Who must change lanes?
choices: The driver in the lane that continues
The driver in the lane that ends
Whichever driver is going slower
Whichever driver turned second
hint: Think about whose lane runs out.
explain: The driver in the lane that ends must move into the available lane using the proper steps for a lane change.
quote: After completing a turn, dual turn lanes may converge into one lane. The driver in the lane that ends must change to the available lane by following the proper steps for a lane change.

q: You plan to turn left using a two-way left turn lane. Which of these is correct?
choices: Enter it close to your turn and watch for oncoming vehicles in it
Enter it well before your turn to get out of the through lanes early
Expect no oncoming vehicles in it, since only your direction may use it
Drive in it for a few blocks to get past slower vehicles
hint: Think about who else may be in this lane, and how long you should be in it.
explain: Only enter a two-way left turn lane close to where you will be turning. Drivers from both directions share it, so watch for oncoming vehicles in your lane.
quote: Vehicles from both directions share this centre lane to turn left. ... Only enter the turning lane close to where you will be turning. Watch for oncoming vehicles in your lane.

q: A two-way left turn lane is separated from your lane by a solid yellow line. May you cross that line to enter the turn lane?
choices: No, you may never cross a solid yellow line
Only if a police officer waves you through
Only at night when traffic is light
Yes, you may cross it to enter the shared turn lane
hint: This lane is meant to be entered from the through lanes.
explain: It is permitted to cross the solid yellow line to enter a shared two-way left turn lane. Enter it only close to where you will turn, and watch for oncoming vehicles in it.
quote: It is permissible to cross the solid yellow line to enter the shared turn lane. Only enter the turning lane close to where you will be turning.

q: May you make a U-turn at an intersection controlled by traffic lights?
choices: Yes, whenever your light is green
Yes, on a red light after a complete stop
Only if a traffic control device permits it
Yes, if no pedestrians are crossing
hint: The lights alone do not give you permission.
explain: U-turns are not permitted at an intersection controlled by traffic lights unless a traffic control device permits it.
quote: U-turns are not permitted: at an intersection controlled by a traffic control signal (traffic lights) unless permitted by a traffic control device

q: In a city, may you make a U-turn in the middle of a block, between intersections?
choices: Yes, if no traffic is coming
Yes, if you signal first
Yes, if the road is wide enough
No, it is not permitted in urban areas
hint: Think about where U-turns are banned in towns and cities.
explain: In urban areas, U-turns are not permitted on a roadway between intersections, at an alley intersection, or at an intersection with a public parking lot access.
quote: In urban areas U-turns are not permitted: on a roadway between intersections

q: On a rural road, a U-turn is not permitted near the crest of a hill if a driver approaching within what distance cannot see you?
choices: 15 metres
50 metres
150 metres
300 metres
hint: It is about one and a half city blocks.
explain: Outside urban areas, U-turns are not permitted on a curve, or on the approach to or near the crest of a hill where a driver within 150 metres cannot see you.
quote: on an approach to or near the crest of a hill where the driver of another vehicle cannot see you that is within 150 metres approaching from either direction.

q: On a rural highway, may you make a U-turn on a curve?
choices: Yes, if you can see 150 metres ahead
Yes, if you turn on your hazard lights
No, U-turns are not permitted on a curve outside urban areas
Yes, if no sign prohibits it
hint: Drivers coming around the bend may not see you in time.
explain: Outside urban areas, U-turns are not permitted on a curve.
quote: Outside urban areas (rural) U-turns are not permitted: on a curve
